summary: Reggae: 60–90 BPM one drop, off-beat skank chords, organ bubble, deep melodic bass
body: Drums: one drop (kick and rim on 3 only), hats swung; steppers for more drive.
Chords: short stabs on every off-beat (the skank) on guitar or piano; organ 'bubble' in 8ths. A chord pattern written as held chords should be shortened to off-beat stabs.
Bass: deep, round, melodic and loud; space between notes.
Harmony: two-chord vamps, i–iv or I–IV.

Apply: pattern/one-drop on the drums, then pattern/prog-reggae-characteristic-1 on the keys four bars later. It leaves tempo and sounds to you: move the tempo toward 60–90 gradually, and swap sounds from the links.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
